items.title: A New Tool Aimed at Solving Synthetic Filmmaking Is Being Unwrapped at Autodesk
items.excerpt: Autodesk is unveiling a 3D Editor and node-based Canvas layer for Flow Studio, letting filmmakers block scenes, direct performance and set camera moves in 3D before generative models render the shot. The pitch is control: adding a 3D component to generative editing to make AI output less 'stodgy and random.'

items.title: Autodesk's New Flow Studio Tools Let Creators Block and Direct AI Shots in 3D
items.excerpt: Autodesk's Flow Studio release adds a 3D Editor plus a node-based 2D Canvas, bringing characters, environments, animation, camera tracks and AI mocap data into one workspace. AWN notes it lays groundwork for expanded Maya/DCC integrations, AI-assisted scene construction and agent-driven directing.

items.title: Snapchat Banning Entirely AI-Generated Videos From Its Spotlight Platform
items.excerpt: Snap is barring fully AI-generated videos from Spotlight, its short-form discovery surface, while still allowing creators to use AI to edit or enhance footage. It draws a distribution-level line between AI-assisted craft and wholly synthetic output.

items.title: Reply AI Film Festival Unveils Jury Featuring 'The Lion King' Director Rob Minkoff
items.excerpt: The Reply AI Film Festival, which runs in tandem with Venice, named a jury including 'The Lion King' director Rob Minkoff and Catherine Hardwicke. Mainstream directors judging AI-made shorts marks another step in generative filmmaking's festival legitimization.

items.title: Venice-Set Reply AI Film Festival Unveils Finalists & Jury
items.excerpt: Deadline details the Reply AI Film Festival's finalist shorts and its jury led by Gabriele Salvatores, with Catherine Hardwicke and Jed Weintrob. Winners are announced on the Lido during the Venice Film Festival.

items.title: Guillermo Del Toro Assures "No Godd*mn AI" Used In 'Pan's Labyrinth' 20th Anniversary Re-Release
items.excerpt: Bringing 'Pan's Labyrinth' back to theaters 20 years on, Del Toro says the restoration stuck to tried-and-true techniques with no AI upscaling or cleanup. It's a pointed craft stance as AI remastering spreads through archive and restoration work.

items.title: Honest Conversations About AI in Film Often Feel Impossible. IndieWire and Andreessen Horowitz Tried Anyway
items.excerpt: IndieWire published video from its Cannes event with a16z, where filmmakers and technologists debated where generative tools actually fit in production. The framing: look at the future without pretending human authorship is optional.

items.title: Venice Chief Alberto Barbera on Hollywood's Festival Retreat, Gender Parity Backslide and the AI Question
items.excerpt: Venice's festival director unpacks his 83rd Biennale lineup and where AI-touched work sits in it, including why Luca Guadagnino's 'Artificial' won't be on the Lido. A gatekeeper's read on how AI films get programmed.

items.title: Tech Reviews: Blender 5, Silhouette 2026 and DaVinci Resolve 21
items.excerpt: Animation Magazine's monthly software review covers Blender 5, Boris FX's Silhouette 2026 and DaVinci Resolve 21 — with Silhouette's machine-learning roto, matting and paint tooling the headline for compositors.

items.title: The rise of the independent AI-assisted developer tools: warnings and considerations
items.excerpt: A look at the wave of solo developers shipping post-production plugins and utilities built with AI coding assistants — and what editors and VFX artists should weigh before putting vibe-coded tools into a paying pipeline.

items.title: Hell Grind | World's First Ever AI Feature Film | Higgsfield Originals (2026)
items.excerpt: Higgsfield premiered 'Hell Grind,' billing it as the first feature-length film generated end-to-end on its AI video platform. It is the clearest public test yet of whether a generative pipeline holds together across feature runtime rather than a 60-second showreel.

items.title: SeedDance 2.5 Just Got Upstaged by Nvidia
items.excerpt: Curious Refuge stress-tests the freshly launched Seedance 2.5 against Nvidia's newest generative video work, comparing shot control, motion coherence and where each model breaks down for narrative filmmaking.

items.title: AI Experts DEBUNK Fake YouTube Channels
items.excerpt: The Corridor Crew brings in AI researchers to pick apart fully synthetic YouTube channels, showing the visual tells that still give generated footage away. A practical detection primer for anyone whose craft now competes with AI slop.
